question: Three independent fits improved the old fivefold regular winner, and three new cold runs opted in to replication. With unused room under 64 fits, should an Agent add two more seeds or stop at three? Register this exercise before the newly qualified course designated score is available.
policy: Use each old 48-fit ordinary winner plus its previously collected two comparison seeds. On its last internal confirmation (excluding the whole exact feature group), calculate the mean and standard error of class-one probability across the three seed-aligned member votes. Explore a further pair only if at least 1% of held rows have distance to the .5 decision boundary less than 1.64 times that Monte Carlo standard error. Keep every originally chosen member at the same weight. If warranted fit new seeds 301147 and 814961 on that same internal partition. On the five-versus-three pilot require the shipped paired score/Brier/diversity test to accept. This research variant concerns binary accuracy only.
assessment: Fit the new seed pair on full training partitions also for a fixed always-five diagnostic. Do not run an extra pilot after failing the uncertainty trigger. Verify all original two added seed controls and initial hard labels against frozen exports, store each completed fit, and seal all five predictions before external scoring. Compare adaptive five versus three seeds, and always-five versus three. Same full fit data, bounded simulated execution <=64. A fresh integration trial warrants pooled adaptive gain >=.002, three positive folds, and no fold worse than -.003; the always-five diagnostic cannot qualify by itself. No model API, designated validation, official test or H2.
